content: Standard React pattern for short one-shot sound-effect/clip playback is a small custom hook (e.g. useAudioClip/usePlaySound) wrapping HTMLAudioElement: create/reuse an Audio instance (often via useRef, or a fresh Audio(src) per play-call for short overlapping clips), call .play() on trigger, and pause()/release refs in a useEffect cleanup on unmount to avoid orphaned playback or memory leaks. For a small keyed clip set, a lookup-map + thin play(key) function is preferred over a full audio-player library (e.g. react-use-audio-player) since there's no scrubbing/seeking/playlist UI need — only trigger-and-play.
